assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemically induced proximity that hijacks the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove a target protein, rather than inhibit it, is a genuine new modality. Heterobifunctional PROTACs and monovalent molecular glues give modular, rational control over recognition and a route to formerly undruggable targets. It changed what chemists and clinicians can do and has spread through chemical biology and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: The 2001 PROTAC proof of concept (Sakamoto, Crews, Deshaies) and the later small-molecule PROTACs are the conceptual core. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains molecular glue degraders. Ciulli's VHL ligands and structural work on ternary complexes are also decisive, so a three-person limit forces a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials, and the mechanism is reproduced independently in hundreds of labs. The field is mature enough for the concept to be recognized, even though approval of a PROTAC drug is still pending. Timing is good but not late.
uncertainties: Whether Ciulli should displace Deshaies or Handa is unresolved.
Clinical benefit of PROTACs is not yet established by approvals; I am relying on memory of trial status and have not verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lipid nanoparticles that encapsulate and deliver nucleic acids made siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines practicable. This is a chemistry-of-materials solution to a delivery problem, using ionizable lipids and controlled self-assembly. It is a clear case of molecular design turned into technology with large societal effect.
assessment.attribution: Cullis, Hope and Madden developed the core encapsulation and ionizable-lipid LNP technology. MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer made major later contributions to optimization and translation. Credit across academic and company teams is entangled and the allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at huge scale and independently reproduced, so confirmation is very strong. Recognition would be timely. Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside-modified mRNA is a framing issue but does not remove the delivery chemistry.
uncertainties: Patent and company disputes may cloud who was decisive.
Which lipid chemistry (ionizable lipid design versus encapsulation process) deserves priority is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as a principle for organizing cells has changed how condensates, membraneless organelles and intrinsically disordered proteins are studied. It connects polymer physical chemistry to cell biology and has strong impact beyond chemistry. It also opens drug-discovery and biomaterials directions.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquids, and Rosen supplied multivalent-interaction and reconstitution frameworks. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded physics. A three-person prize is plausible but leaves out theoretically important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Concept is widely adopted, but debate remains over which cellular condensates are functionally phase-separated, and some in-cell evidence is contested. Moderately mature, perhaps a little early for the full picture.
uncertainties: Controversy over in vivo relevance and over artefacts from overexpression.
Whether this is better read as chemistry or as cell biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors perform direct chemical conversion of single nucleotides (deaminase chemistry) in living cells without double-strand breaks, and can be directed with high precision. It is a clear example of protein engineering and molecular design creating a tool that clinicians now use. Therapeutic editing in patients adds weight.
assessment.attribution: Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor) did the decisive experimental work in the Liu lab, with Liu as intellectual lead. Nishida and Kondo's independent deaminase-based editing is a related but different line. A single-laureate or Liu-led configuration is easy to justify.
assessment.maturity: Clinical first-in-human results are emerging and many labs have independently reproduced the method. It follows the 2020 CRISPR Chemistry prize, so timing could be seen as slightly early or as an obvious follow-on.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with Nishida and Kondo.
Long-term safety and off-target deamination are still being studied.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single nucleic-acid molecules electrically through protein or solid-state pores created a new analytical measurement and a commercial long-read sequencing technology. It rests on molecular engineering of pores and on single-molecule sensing, which resonates with my own sensor background.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton conceived the idea of threading DNA through a pore, Kasianowicz showed polynucleotide transport through alpha-hemolysin, Bayley engineered pores for sensing and Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled movement. Several people were decisive and a three-person limit is awkward.
assessment.maturity: Widely used in genomics and diagnostics, and independently confirmed. Long-read accuracy improvements are ongoing. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Strong competition among at least five contributors for three slots.
Part of the impact is sequencing rather than chemistry in the narrow sense.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programming nanoparticle assembly with DNA, and the later spherical nucleic acids, give sequence-encoded control over nanoscale structure and over cellular uptake and sensing. Colorimetric detection and intracellular gene regulation are good examples of a molecular-design principle moving into diagnostics. This sits close to my own work on nanoparticle biosensing.
assessment.attribution: The 1996 papers from Mirkin and Alivisatos were independent and simultaneous. Mirkin's subsequent spherical nucleic acid work is the main driver of translation. Storhoff and Mucic were important coauthors but are not natural prize recipients.
assessment.maturity: Concept reproduced widely, and clinical translation of spherical nucleic acids is still modest. A mixed picture: well confirmed as a tool, still developing as a therapy.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is limited so far.
Alivisatos is also credited for quantum dots, which may complicate framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive chemical probes to read functional enzyme states directly in complex proteomes, enabling inhibitor discovery and target identification. It has influenced chemical proteomics and drug discovery, and has links to covalent-drug design.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the central figure, with Bogyo and Overkleeft as major developers of probes for protease classes. Weerapana's cysteine reactivity profiling is a later extension. Fair credit is possible, but it requires picking between several strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Established and widely used, with independent adoption in academia and pharma. The impact is more as a technology platform than a single transformative concept, and it is long mature.
uncertainties: Whether the field reads as a single discovery or a set of probe technologies.
Role of the covalent-fragment screening line is not fully clear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically encoding noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets chemists place new chemistry into proteins in living cells. It gives precise molecular control, with applications in biophysical probes, bioconjugation and biotherapeutics. It is a strong example of design principles that spread to biomedicine and materials.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the approach in bacteria and in eukaryotes, and Chin extended it to multiple codons and engineered ribosomes. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama are also decisive in specific systems. Allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Method is robust and widely reproduced. Clinical products such as site-specific antibody-drug conjugates are emerging. Timely but not urgent.
uncertainties: Several credible contributors compete for two or three slots.
